source.markdown: # ABSTRACT
source.text: ABSTRACT

blocks.text: ABSTRACT

target.markdown: ## 摘要

source.markdown: Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) are commonly integrated with computing devices to enhance the performance and capabilities of graphical workloads. In addition, they are increasingly being integrated in data centers and clouds such that they can be used to accelerate data intensive workloads. Under a number of scenarios the GPU can be shared between multiple applications at a fine granularity allowing a spy application to monitor side channels and attempt to infer the behavior of the victim. For example, OpenGL and WebGL send workloads to the GPU at the granularity of a frame, allowing an attacker to interleave the use of the GPU to measure the side-effects of the victim computation through performance counters or other resource tracking APIs. We demonstrate the vulnerability using two applications. First, we show that an OpenGL based spy can fingerprint websites accurately, track user activities within the website, and even infer the keystroke timings for a password text box with high accuracy. The second application demonstrates how a CUDA spy application can derive the internal parameters of a neural network model being used by another CUDA application, illustrating these threats on the cloud. To counter these attacks, the paper suggests mitigations based on limiting the rate of the calls, or limiting the granularity of the returned information.

target.markdown: 图形处理器（GPU）通常与计算设备集成，以增强图形工作负载的性能和能力。此外，它们越来越多地被集成到数据中心和云中，从而可以用于加速数据密集型工作负载。在许多场景下，GPU 可以被多个应用程序细粒度地共享，这使得间谍应用程序能够监视侧信道并尝试推断受害者的行为。例如，OpenGL 和 WebGL 以帧为粒度向 GPU 发送工作负载，允许攻击者交错使用 GPU，通过性能计数器或其他资源跟踪 API 来测量受害者计算的副作用。我们使用两个应用程序演示了这种漏洞。首先，我们展示了一个基于 OpenGL 的间谍程序可以准确地指纹识别网站、跟踪用户在网站内的活动，甚至可以高精度地推断密码文本框的击键时间。第二个应用程序演示了 CUDA 间谍应用程序如何推导出另一个 CUDA 应用程序正在使用的神经网络模型的内部参数，说明了这些威胁在云环境中的存在。为了应对这些攻击，本文提出了基于限制调用速率或限制返回信息粒度的缓解措施。

target.markdown: ## 1 引言

source.markdown: Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) are integral components to most modern computing devices, used to optimize the performance of today's graphics and multi-media heavy workloads. They are also increasingly integrated on computing servers to accelerate a range of applications from domains including security, computer vision, computational finance, bio-informatics and many others [52]. Both these classes of applications can operate on sensitive data [25, 31, 57] which can be compromised by security vulnerabilities in the GPU stack.

target.markdown: 图形处理器（GPU）是大多数现代计算设备的重要组成部分，用于优化当今图形和多媒体密集型工作负载的性能。它们越来越多地集成在计算服务器上，以加速包括安全、计算机视觉、计算金融、生物信息学等众多领域的广泛应用[52]。这两类应用都可能处理敏感数据[25, 31, 57]，而这些数据可能会因 GPU 栈中的安全漏洞而遭到泄露。

source.markdown: Although the security of GPUs is only starting to be explored, several vulnerabilities have already been demonstrated [46, 49, 55, 58, 63, 71, 74]. Most related to this paper, Luo et al. demonstrated a timing channel from the CPU side timing a GPU operation. In particular, they assume that the GPU is running an encryption library, and time encryption of chosen text blocks. The encryption runtime varies depending on the encryption key: the memory access patterns are key-dependent causing timing differences due to GPU memory coalescing effects enabling a timing side channel attack on the key [40]. In [40], the attacker needs to launch the encryption kernel on GPU and measure the whole kernel execution time on its own process (on CPU side), totally different than our threat model that investigates side channel between two concurrent apps on the GPU. More recently, Naghibijouybari et al. showed that covert channels between colluding concurrently running CUDA applications (CUDA is Nvidia's programming language for general purpose workloads on the GPU [4]) on a GPU may be constructed [54, 55]. Neither of these papers demonstrates a general side channel attack, which is the focus of this paper.

target.markdown: 虽然 GPU 安全性方面的研究才刚刚起步，但已有若干漏洞被相继披露[46, 49, 55, 58, 63, 71, 74]。与本文最相关的是，Luo 等人展示了从 CPU 侧对 GPU 操作进行计时的时序信道。具体而言，他们假设 GPU 正在运行加密库，并对选定文本块的加密过程进行计时。加密运行时间会因加密密钥的不同而变化：内存访问模式与密钥相关，由于 GPU 内存合并效应而产生计时差异，从而实现针对密钥的计时侧信道攻击[40]。在文献[40]中，攻击者需要在 GPU 上启动加密内核，并在其自身进程（CPU 端）中测量整个内核的执行时间，这与本文所研究的在 GPU 上两个并发应用之间的侧信道威胁模型完全不同。最近，Naghibijouybari 等人表明，在 GPU 上勾结并发运行的 CUDA 应用（CUDA 是英伟达用于 GPU 通用计算工作负载的编程语言[4]）之间可以构建隐蔽信道[54, 55]。但上述工作均未展示本文所重点研究的一般性侧信道攻击。

source.markdown: This paper explores whether side channel attacks on GPUs are practical. GPUs often process sensitive data both with respect to graphics workloads (which render the screen and can expose user information and activity) and computational workloads (which may include applications with sensitive data or algorithms). If indeed possible, such attacks represent a novel and dangerous threat vector. There are a number of unique aspects of side channel attacks on the GPU due to the different computational model, high degree of parallelism, unique co-location and sharing properties, as well as attacker-measurable channels present in the GPU stack. We show that indeed side channels are present and exploitable, and demonstrate attacks on a range of Nvidia GPUs and for both graphics and computational software stacks and applications.

target.markdown: 本文探讨针对 GPU 的侧信道攻击是否切实可行。GPU 经常处理敏感数据，无论是在图形工作负载（负责屏幕渲染，可能暴露用户信息和活动）还是在计算工作负载（可能包含涉及敏感数据或算法的应用）中皆是如此。若此类攻击确实可行，则代表一种新颖而危险的威胁向量。由于 GPU 具有不同的计算模型、高度并行性、独特的共置与共享特性，以及 GPU 栈中存在的攻击者可测量的信道，针对 GPU 的侧信道攻击具有许多独特之处。我们证明了此类侧信道确实存在且可被利用，并在多种英伟达 GPU 上针对图形和计算两种软件栈及应用演示了攻击。

target.markdown: 测量受害者在英伟达 GPU 图形栈和计算栈中的侧信道行为。在 OpenGL 工作负载场景中，我们发现只要资源足以支持，内核（着色器程序）就可以被并发调度。我们还验证了对于相互竞争的 CUDA 操作系统同样适用。最后，当工作负载同时来自 CUDA 和 OpenGL 时，它们以更细的并发粒度（在计算内核粒度上交叉执行）交替使用 GPU。我们将针对每种攻击类型讨论其共置的可能性。

source.markdown: Armed with the co-location knowledge, we demonstrate a family of attacks where the spy can interleave execution with the victim to extract side channel information. We explore using (1) Memory allocation APIs; (2) GPU performance counters; and (3) Time measurement as possible sources of leakage. We show that all three sources leak side channel information regarding the behavior of the victim. We successfully build three practical and dangerous end-to-end attacks on several generations of Nvidia GPUs.

target.markdown: 在掌握共置条件的基础上，我们展示了一系列攻击，攻击者（间谍进程）能够与受害者进程交叉执行以提取侧信道信息。我们探索了三种可能的泄漏来源：（1）内存分配 API；（2）GPU 性能计数器；（3）时间测量。我们证明这三种来源均会泄漏关于受害者行为的侧信道信息。我们成功地在多代英伟达 GPU 上构建了三种实用且危险的端到端攻击。

source.markdown: To illustrate attacks on graphics applications we implement a web-fingerprinting attack that identifies user browsing websites with high accuracy. We show an extension to this attack that tracks user activity on a website, and captures keystroke timing. We also illustrate attacks on computational workloads showing that a spy can reconstruct the internal structure of a neural network with high accuracy by collecting side channel information through the performance counters on the GPU.

target.markdown: 为了说明针对图形应用程序的攻击，我们实现了一种网页指纹识别攻击，能够高精度地识别用户正在浏览的网站。我们进一步扩展了该攻击，使其能够跟踪用户在网站上的活动并捕获击键时序。我们还展示了针对计算工作负载的攻击：通过收集 GPU 性能计数器中的侧信道信息，间谍进程能够高精度地重构神经网络的内部结构。

source.markdown: We explore possible mitigation to this type of attack. Preventing or containing contention on GPUs by allocating them exclusively or changing their design could limit the leakage, but is likely impractical. Thus, we focus on limiting the attacker's ability to measure the leakage. We show that solutions that interfere with the measurement accuracy can substantially limit the leakage and interfere with the attacker's ability to extract sensitive information.

target.markdown: ## 2.1 GPU 编程接口

source.markdown: GPUs were originally designed to accelerate graphics and multimedia workloads. They are usually programmed using application programming interfaces such as OpenGL for 2D/3D graphics [17], or WebGL [20] which is usable within browsers. We call OpenGL/WebGL and similar interfaces the graphics stack of the GPU. OpenGL is accessible by any application on a desktop with user level privileges making all attacks practical on a desktop. In theory, a JavaScript application may launch the attack using WebGL, but we found that current versions of WebGL do not expose measurement APIs that allow leakage.

target.markdown: GPU 最初是为加速图形和多媒体工作负载而设计的。它们通常使用应用程序编程接口进行编程，例如用于二维/三维图形的 OpenGL [17]，或可在浏览器中使用的 WebGL [20]。我们将 OpenGL/WebGL 及类似接口称为 GPU 的图形栈。在桌面系统中，任何具有用户级权限的应用程序都可以访问 OpenGL，这使得所有攻击在桌面系统上都具有实际可行性。理论上，JavaScript 应用程序可以利用 WebGL 发起攻击，但我们发现当前版本的 WebGL 并未暴露可用于泄漏信息的测量接口。

source.markdown: In the past few years, GPU manufacturers have also enabled general purpose programmability for GPUs, allowing them to be used to accelerate data intensive applications using programming interfaces such as CUDA [4], Vulkan [19] and OpenCL [13]. We call this alternative interface/software stack for accessing the GPU the computational stack. Computational GPU programs are used widely on computational clusters, and cloud computing systems to accelerate data intensive applications [6]. These systems typically do not process graphics workloads at all since the machines are used as computational servers without direct graphical output. Nowadays, most non-cloud systems also support general purpose computing on GPUs [3] and are increasingly moving towards GPU concurrent multiprogramming.

source.markdown: We briefly review the GPU architecture to provide some insight into its execution model and how contention arises. The architecture also illustrates that due to the high parallelism and small shared caches, conventional CPU attacks such as prime-probe cache attacks are virtually impossible; it is difficult to correlate accesses to the potential thousands of concurrently executing threads that may have generated them.

# GPU Architecture and CUDA Execution Model

## (a) GPU Hardware Architecture Overview

### Top-Level Components

- **GigaThread Engine**  
  - Manages thread scheduling across the entire GPU.

- **Memory Controllers** (x4, two on each side)  
  - Interface between GPU cores and external memory (e.g., GDDR).

- **GPCs (Graphics Processing Clusters)** — 4 total (2 top, 2 bottom)  
  Each GPC contains:
  - **Raster Engine**
  - **SMs (Streaming Multiprocessors)** — 4 per GPC → Total 16 SMs shown

- **L2 Cache**  
  - Shared cache layer connecting all GPCs and memory controllers.

> *Note: Dashed lines indicate logical or data flow connections from GPCs to detailed SM view.*

---

## Detailed View of a Single Streaming Multiprocessor (SM)

Each SM is composed of:

### Instruction & Control Units
- **Instruction Cache**
- **Warp Scheduler** ×2
- **Dispatch Unit** ×2

### Register File
- Central register file shared among cores in the SM.

### Compute Units (per row, multiple rows implied by “⋮”)
Each compute unit group includes:
- **Core** ×2
- **LD/ST** (Load/Store unit)
- **SFU** (Special Function Unit)

### Memory Hierarchy within SM
- **Shared Memory / L1 Cache**
- **Texture Units (Tex)** ×4
- **Texture Cache**
- **Polymorph Engine** (handles geometry processing tasks)

> *This SM structure is replicated across all 16 SMs in the full GPU diagram.*

---

## (b) CUDA Application Execution Model

### Host (CPU) Side
- **CUDA Application**
  - Contains kernels: `Kernel 1`, `Kernel 2`, ...

### Device (GPU) Side

#### Thread Blocks
- Multiple **Thread Blocks** are launched on the GPU.
- Each block consists of multiple warps (shown as groups of threads with arrows indicating execution flow).

#### Warps
- Each warp contains **32 threads** (as labeled in zoomed-in view).
- Warps are scheduled onto SMs for parallel execution.
- Threads within a warp execute in lockstep (SIMT model).

> *Dashed line separates Host (CPU) and Device (GPU), indicating communication boundary via PCIe or similar interface.*

---

## Summary Diagram Labels

| Section | Label |
|--------|-------|
| Left large box | **GPU** |
| Right upper box | **Host (CPU)** |
| Right middle box | **Device (GPU)** |
| Bottom right inset | **Warps** (each containing 32 threads) |
| Middle vertical panel | **SM** (detailed internal structure) |

---

## Key Observations

- The architecture follows a hierarchical design:  
  `GPU → GPC → SM → Core/Warp → Thread`

- CUDA applications launch kernels that map to thread blocks, which are further divided into warps executed on SMs.

- Memory hierarchy spans from global (via Memory Controller) → L2 → Shared/L1 → Registers.

- Specialized units like SFU, Tex, Polymorph Engine handle non-arithmetic operations efficiently.

source.markdown: Figure 1a presents an architecture overview of a typical GPU. There are a number of resources that are shared between threads based on where they are mapped within the GPU. The GPU consists of a number of Graphical Processing Clusters (GPCs) which include some graphics units like raster engine and a number of Streaming Multiprocessor (SM) cores. Each SM has several L1 caches (for the instructions, global data, constant data and texture data). They are all shared among the computational threads mapped to it. There is a globally shared L2 cache to provide faster access to memory. As a typical example, the Nvidia Tesla K40, includes 15 SMs [11]. The size of the global memory, L2 cache, constant memory and shared memory are 12 GB, 1.5 MB, 64 KB and 48 KB respectively.

source.markdown: The GPU memory is shared across all the SMs and is connected to the chip using several high speed channels (see memory controllers in Figure 1a), resulting in bandwidths of several hundred gigabytes per second, but with a high latency. The impact of the latency is hidden partially using caches, but more importantly, the large number of warps/threads ensures the availability of ready warps to take up the available processing bandwidth when other warps are stalled waiting for memory. This results in fine granularity and frequent interleaving of executing groups of threads, making it difficult to correlate fine-grained side channel leakage (e.g., cache miss on a cache set) to a particular computation source.

source.markdown: Figure 2 demonstrates the logical graphics pipeline. The vertex shader program executes per-vertex processing, including transforming the vertex 3D position into a screen position. The geometry shader program executes per-primitive processing and can add or drop primitives. The setup and rasterization unit translates vector representations of the image (from the geometric primitives used by the geometry shader) to a pixel representation of the same shapes. The fragment (pixel) shader program performs per-pixel processing, including texturing, and coloring. The output of graphics workloads consists of the pixel colors of the final image and is computed in fragment shader. The fragment shader makes extensive use of sampled and filtered lookups into large 1D, 2D, or 3D arrays called textures, which are stored in the GPU global memory. The contention among the different threads carrying out operations on the image is dependent on the image. When measuring performance counters or memory usage, these values leak information about the graphics workload being rendered by the GPU.

source.markdown: Thus, instead of targeting fine-grained contention behavior, most of our attacks focus on aggregate measures of contention through available resource tracking APIs. There are a number of mechanisms available to the attacker to measure the victim's performance. These include: (1) the memory allocation API, which exposes the amount of available physical memory on the GPU; (2) the GPU hardware performance counters; and (3) Timing operations while executing concurrently with the victim. We verified that the memory channel is available on both Nvidia [15] and AMD GPUs [14] and on any Operating System supporting OpenGL (including Linux, Windows, and MacOS). Nvidia GPUs currently support performance counters on Linux, Windows and MacOS for computing applications [10] and on Linux and Android [8, 18] for graphics applications, while AMD supports Linux and Windows [7]. WebGL does not appear to offer extensions to measure any of the three channels and therefore cannot be used to implement a spy for our attacks. Although web browsers and websites which use WebGL (as a JavaScript API to use GPU for rendering) can be targeted as victims in our attacks from an OpenGL spy.

source.markdown: Measuring GPU Memory Allocation: When the GPU is used for rendering, a content-related pattern (depending on the size and shape of the object) of memory allocations is performed on the GPU. We can probe the available physical GPU memory using an Nvidia provided API through either a CUDA or an OpenGL context. source.markdown: **Measuring Performance Counters:** We use the Nvidia profiling tools [10] to monitor the GPU performance counters from a CUDA spy [8]. Table 1 summarizes some of the important events/metrics tracked by the GPU categorized into five general groups: memory, instruction, multiprocessor, cache and texture. Although the GPU allows an application to only observe the counters related to its own computational kernel, these are affected by the execution of a victim kernel: for example, if the victim kernel accesses the cache, it may replace the spy's data allowing the spy to observe a cache miss (through cache-related counters). We note that OpenGL also offers an interface to query the performance counters enabling them to be sampled by a graphics-based spy.

source.markdown: We launch two long running graphics applications rendering an object on the screen repeatedly. Each thread is responsible for assigning color to each pixel in fragment shader. We need to know about SM-ID and timing information of each thread on each OpenGL workload to evaluate contention. OpenGL developers (Khronos group) provide two extensions: "NV_shader_thread_group" [16] which enable programmers to query the ThreadID, the WarpID and the SM-ID in OpenGL shader codes and "ARB_shader_clock" [2] which exposes local timing information within a single shader invocation. We used these two extensions during the reverse engineering phase in the fragment shader code to obtain this information. Since OpenGL does not provide facilities to directly query execution state, we encode this information in the colors (R, G, B values) of the output pixels of the shader program (since the color of pixels is the only output of shader program). On the application side, we read the color of each pixel from the framebuffer using the glReadPixels() method and decode the colors to obtain the encoded ThreadID, SM-ID and timing information of each pixel (representing a thread).

target.markdown: 我们启动两个长时间运行的图形应用程序，反复在屏幕上渲染一个对象。每个线程负责在片段着色器中为每个像素分配颜色。我们需要了解每个 OpenGL 工作负载上各线程的 SM-ID 和计时信息，以评估争用情况。OpenGL 的开发方（Khronos 联盟）提供了两个扩展："NV_shader_thread_group" [16] 使程序员能够在 OpenGL 着色器代码中查询 ThreadID、WarpID 和 SM-ID，以及 "ARB_shader_clock" [2] 暴露单次着色器调用内的本地计时信息。在逆向工程阶段，我们在片段着色器代码中使用了这两个扩展来获取这些信息。由于 OpenGL 并不提供直接查询执行状态的机制，我们将这些信息编码到着色器程序输出像素的颜色（R、G、B 值）中（因为像素颜色是着色器程序的唯一输出）。在应用程序侧，我们使用 glReadPixels() 方法从帧缓冲区中读取每个像素的颜色，并对颜色进行解码，从而获得每个像素（代表一个线程）的 ThreadID、SM-ID 和计时信息。

source.markdown: We observed that two graphics applications whose workloads do not exceed the GPU hardware resources can collocate concurrently. Only if a single kernel can exhaust the resources of an entire GPU (extremely unlikely), the second kernel would have to wait. Typically, a GPU thread is allocated to each pixel, and therefore, the amount of resources reserved by each graphics kernel depends on the size of the object being processed by the GPU. We observe that a spy can co-locate with a rendering application even if renders the full screen (Resolution 1920x1080) on our system. Because the spy does not ask for many resources (number of threads, shared memory, etc...), we also discover that it is able to share an SM with the other application. In the next two subsections, we explain implementation of two end to end attacks on the graphics stack of GPU.

target.markdown: 我们观察到，两个图形应用程序在其工作负载不超过 GPU 硬件资源的情况下可以并发共置。只有当单个内核耗尽了整个 GPU 的资源时（这种情况极不可能发生），第二个内核才必须等待。通常，GPU 会为每个像素分配一个线程，因此每个图形内核所预留的资源量取决于 GPU 所处理对象的大小。我们观察到，即使受害者应用程序以全屏（分辨率 1920x1080）进行渲染，间谍程序仍能与之共置。由于间谍程序不会请求大量资源（线程数、共享内存等），我们还发现它能够与其他应用程序共享同一个 SM。在接下来的两个小节中，我们将阐述针对 GPU 图形栈的两个端到端攻击的实现。

source.markdown: and User Interface (UI) process. By default, Chrome does not use the GPU to rasterize the web content (recall that rasterization is the conversion from a geometric description of the image, to the pixel description). In particular, the webpage content is rendered by default in the renderer process on the CPU. Chrome uses shared memory with the GPU process to facilitate fast exchange of data. The GPU process reads the CPU-rasterized images of the web content and uploads it to the GPU memory. The GPU process next issues OpenGL draw calls to draw several equal-sized quads, which are each a rectangle containing the final bitmap image for the tile. Finally, Chrome's compositor composites all the images together with the browser's UI using the GPU.

source.markdown: We note that WebGL enables websites and browsers to use GPU for whole rendering pipeline, making our attacks effective for all websites that use WebGL [20]. Based on WebGL statistics [22] 98% of visitors to a series of websites used WebGL enabled browsers and [71] report that at least 53% of the top-100 sites, and 16.4% of the top-10,000 sites use WebGL. For websites that do not use WebGL, Chrome does not use the GPU for rasterization by default, but there is an option that users can set in the browser to enable GPU rasterization.$^1$ If hardware rasterization is enabled, all polygons are rendered using OpenGL primitives (triangles and lines) on the GPU. GPU accelerated drawing and rasterization can offer substantially better performance, especially to render web pages that require frequently updated portions of screen. GPU accelerated rendering allows for more seamless animations and better performance, while freeing up the CPU. As a result, the Chromium Project's GPU Architecture Roadmap [5] seeks to enable GPU accelerated rasterization by default in Chrome in the near future. For our attacks we assume that hardware rasterization is enabled but we also report the experimental results without enabling GPU rasterization.

target.markdown: 我们注意到，WebGL 使网站和浏览器能够使用 GPU 完成整个渲染流水线，从而使我们的攻击对所有使用 WebGL 的网站均有效 [20]。根据 WebGL 统计数据 [22]，在某系列网站的访客中，有 98% 使用了支持 WebGL 的浏览器；文献 [71] 报告称，排名前 100 的网站中至少有 53%、排名前 10,000 的网站中有 16.4% 使用了 WebGL。对于不使用 WebGL 的网站，Chrome 默认并不使用 GPU 进行光栅化，但用户可以在浏览器中设置一个选项以启用 GPU 光栅化。$^1$ 如果启用了硬件光栅化，所有多边形都将通过 GPU 上的 OpenGL 图元（三角形和直线）进行渲染。GPU 加速的绘制与光栅化能够带来显著的性能提升，尤其对于需要频繁更新屏幕部分内容的网页渲染而言更是如此。GPU 加速渲染可以实现更流畅的动画效果和更佳的性能，同时释放 CPU 资源。因此，Chromium 项目的 GPU 架构路线图 [5] 致力于在不久的将来默认在 Chrome 中启用 GPU 加速光栅化。对于我们的攻击，我们假设已启用硬件光栅化，但也会报告在未启用 GPU 光栅化情况下的实验结果。

source.markdown: **Launching the Attack:** In this attack, a spy has to be active while the GPU is being used as a user is browsing the Internet. In the most likely attack scenario, a user application uses OpenGL from a malicious user level App on a desktop, to create a spy to infer the behavior of a browser process as it uses the GPU. However, a CUDA (or OpenCL) spy is also possible assuming the corresponding driver and software environment is installed on the system, enabling Graphics-CUDA side channel attack described in Section 6.

# 内存分配事件大小分析（Google.com, Amazon.com, Facebook.com）

## 图 (a) Google.com

- **横轴**：Memory Allocation Event（内存分配事件编号），范围 0–50
- **纵轴**：Size (KB)（分配大小，单位 KB），范围 0–5000
- **数据特征**：
  - 大部分事件分配大小为 0 或接近 0。
  - 在事件 ~13、~17、~20、~26、~30、~32、~34 处出现显著峰值。
  - 最高峰值出现在事件 ~18，约为 **4100 KB**。
  - 其余峰值多在 **1900–2000 KB** 区间。
  - 整体呈现稀疏突发式分配模式。

## 图 (b) Amazon.com

- **横轴**：Memory Allocation Event（内存分配事件编号），范围 0–120
- **纵轴**：Size (KB)（分配大小，单位 KB），范围 0–5000
- **数据特征**：
  - 分配事件更密集，覆盖整个时间跨度。
  - 多个高峰值：事件 ~22 达到约 **4100 KB**；事件 ~25、~30、~35、~55、~70、~80、~95、~105、~110 等均有明显峰值。
  - 多数峰值集中在 **1900–2300 KB** 区间。
  - 存在连续小幅度波动和平台期（如事件 40–50、80–90）。
  - 显示高频、多峰、持续性内存分配行为。

## 图 (c) Facebook.com

- **横轴**：Memory Allocation Event（内存分配事件编号），范围 0–50
- **纵轴**：Size (KB)（分配大小，单位 KB），范围 0–5000
- **数据特征**：
  - 初始阶段（事件 0–12）几乎无分配。
  - 事件 ~14–16 出现两个约 **1900 KB** 的峰值。
  - 事件 ~22 出现最高峰值，约 **4100 KB**。
  - 后续事件 ~26、~30、~34、~38–42 出现多个 **1900–2000 KB** 峰值。
  - 事件 45 后回归零值。
  - 呈现集中爆发型分配，中间有短暂静默期。

source.markdown: **Classification:** We first experimented with using time-series classification through dynamic time warping, but the training and classification complexity was high. Instead, we construct features from the full time series signal and use traditional machine learning classification, which also achieved better accuracy. In particular, we compute several statistical features, including minimum, maximum, mean, standard deviation, slope, skew and kurtosis, for the series of memory allocations collected through the side channel when a website is loading. We selected these features because they are easy to compute and capture the essence of the distribution of the time series values. The skew and kurtosis capture the shape of the distribution of the time series. Skew characterizes the degree of asymmetry of values, while the Kurtosis measures the relative peakness or flatness of the distribution relative to a normal distribution [56]. We computed these features separately for the first and the second half of the timeseries recorded for each website. We further divided the data in each half into 3 equal segments, and measured the slope and the average of each segment. We also added the number of memory allocations for each website, referred as "memallocated", into the feature vector representing a website. This process resulted in the feature set consisting of 37 features.

target.markdown: **分类：** 我们首先尝试使用基于动态时间规整的时间序列分类方法，但其训练和分类复杂度较高。因此，我们改用从完整时间序列信号中构建特征，并结合传统机器学习分类方法，该方法也取得了更高的准确率。具体而言，我们针对通过侧信道在网站加载过程中采集到的内存分配序列，计算了若干统计特征，包括最小值、最大值、均值、标准差、斜率、偏度和峰度。我们选择这些特征是因为它们易于计算，并且能够刻画时间序列值分布的本质。其中，偏度和峰度用于刻画时间序列分布的形状：偏度表征数据值分布的不对称程度，而峰度则衡量分布相对于正态分布的尖峭或平坦程度 [56]。我们针对每个网站所记录时间序列的前半段和后半段分别计算了上述特征。我们进一步将每半段数据划分为 3 个等长的子段，并分别计算各子段的斜率与平均值。此外，我们还将每个网站的内存分配次数（记为 "memallocated"）加入了用于表示该网站的特征向量中。经过上述过程，我们最终得到一个由 37 个特征构成的特征集。

We evaluate the performance of these models to identify the best performing classifier for our dataset. For this and all classification experiments we validated the classification models using standard 10-fold cross-validation method [44] (which separates the training and testing data in every instance).

target.markdown: 随后，我们利用这些特征，基于三种标准机器学习算法构建了分类模型，分别是采用 3 个近邻的 K 近邻算法（KNN-3）、高斯朴素贝叶斯（NB）以及包含 100 个估计器的随机森林（RF）。我们评估了这些模型的性能，以找出针对我们数据集表现最佳的分类器。对于本次以及所有的分类实验，我们均采用标准的 10 折交叉验证方法 [44] 来验证分类模型（在每一折中分别划分训练集与测试集）。

source.markdown: As performance measures of these classifiers, we computed the precision (Prec), recall (Rec), and F-measure (FM) for machine learning classification models. Prec refers to the accuracy of the system in rejecting the negative classes while the Rec is the accuracy of the system in accepting positive classes. Low recall leads to high rejection of positive instances (false negatives) while low precision leads to high acceptance of negative instances (false positives). FM represents a balance between precision and recall.

target.markdown: 作为这些分类器的性能指标，我们计算了机器学习分类模型的精确率（Prec）、召回率（Rec）和 F 值（FM）。Prec 指的是系统在拒绝负类时的准确率，而 Rec 指的是系统在接受正类时的准确率。较低的召回率会导致大量正类实例被拒绝（假阴性），而较低的精确率则会导致大量负类实例被错误接受（假阳性）。FM 则体现了精确率与召回率之间的平衡。

source.markdown: **Generalization across screen sizes:** We considered full screen browser window in our experiments. Given that different users may have different size browser windows, we wanted to check if the attack generalizes across window sizes. We discover that changing the window size results in a similar signal with different amplitude for most websites, and for responsive websites that have dynamic content or do not scale with window size, there is some variance in the memory allocation signal (e.g., some objects missing due to smaller window). By training the ML model using full screen data and testing with window size 1280*810 and 800*600 measurements, we still see average accuracy of 82% and 63% respectively. We believe performance can also be improved by training with measurements at different window sizes.

target.markdown: **跨屏幕尺寸的泛化：** 在实验中，我们使用的是全屏浏览器窗口。考虑到不同用户可能使用不同尺寸的浏览器窗口，我们希望验证该攻击能否在不同窗口尺寸之间进行泛化。我们发现，对于大多数网站而言，改变窗口大小会使信号呈现出相似的形态，但幅度有所不同；而对于具有动态内容或不会随窗口大小缩放的自适应网站，其内存分配信号则会存在一定的差异（例如，由于窗口较小，部分对象缺失）。我们使用全屏数据训练机器学习模型，并分别使用窗口尺寸为 1280×810 和 800×600 时采集的数据进行测试，结果仍分别获得了 82% 和 63% 的平均准确率。我们相信，通过在不同窗口尺寸下采集数据进行训练，可以进一步提高其性能。

# 内存分配事件与大小关系图分析

本部分包含两个子图（a）和（b），分别展示不同用户操作场景下的内存分配事件（Memory Allocation Event）与其对应分配大小（Size, KB）的关系。每个数据点以蓝色圆点表示，并通过垂直线连接至 x 轴，形成“茎叶”状可视化效果。

---

## 图 (a)：Signing-In 与 Account Page 操作

### 坐标轴说明：
- **X 轴**：`Memory Allocation Event` —— 表示内存分配发生的序号或时间戳（单位：事件编号），范围从 0 到 600。
- **Y 轴**：`Size (KB)` —— 表示每次内存分配的大小（单位：千字节），范围从 0 到 16000 KB。

### 标注区域：
1. **→ Signing-In**
   - 位于图表右上部，指向一组高密度、高幅值的内存分配事件。
   - 对应 X 轴约 250–400 区间，Y 值集中在 14000–15000 KB。
   - 特征：大量重复性高内存分配，可能代表登录过程中加载资源或初始化会话。

2. **→ Account Page**
   - 位于图表右侧中部，指向一个孤立的中等高度峰值。
   - 对应 X 轴约 430 处，Y 值约为 7500 KB。
   - 特征：单次较大内存分配，可能为账户页面渲染或数据加载。

### 数据分布特征：
- 在 X=0–100 区间：存在多个低幅值（<4000 KB）和小幅波动分配。
- 在 X=100–200 区间：出现一次显著下降后回升，中间有零星小分配。
- 在 X=200–400 区间：密集高峰区，多数分配 >14000 KB，符合 “Signing-In” 标注。
- 在 X=400–500 区间：除 “Account Page” 外，其余多为 <2000 KB 的小分配。
- X>500 后无数据点。

---

## 图 (b)：Open an Account 与 Check&Saving 操作

### 坐标轴说明：
- **X 轴**：`Memory Allocation Event` —— 同上，范围从 0 到 500。
- **Y 轴**：`Size (KB)` —— 同上，但上限扩展至 18000 KB。

### 标注区域：
1. **→ Open an Account**
   - 位于图表右中部，指向一组极高且密集的内存分配。
   - 对应 X 轴约 250–320 区间，Y 值集中在 14000–15000 KB。
   - 特征：类似图(a)中的“Signing-In”，但起始更早、持续时间略短，可能为开户流程中加载表单、验证模块等。

2. **→ Check&Saving**
   - 位于图表右侧偏下，指向一个独立的高耸尖峰。
   - 对应 X 轴约 400 处，Y 值达到约 16000 KB（接近 Y 轴最大值）。
   - 特征：单次极大内存分配，可能涉及支票/储蓄账户数据结构初始化或大额缓存加载。

### 数据分布特征：
- 在 X=0–100 区间：多个低至中等幅值分配（<4000 KB），部分达 9000 KB。
- 在 X=100–200 区间：波动频繁，最高约 12000 KB，最低接近 0。
- 在 X=200–320 区间：“Open an Account” 主导，持续高负载。
- 在 X=320–400 区间：短暂回落，随后在 X≈400 出现“Check&Saving”极端峰值。
- X>400 后仍有少量小分配，直至 X=450 左右结束。

---

## 对比总结

| 维度             | 图 (a)                          | 图 (b)                          |
|------------------|----------------------------------|----------------------------------|
| 主要操作         | Signing-In, Account Page        | Open an Account, Check&Saving   |
| 最大内存分配     | ~15000 KB                       | ~16000 KB                       |
| 高密度区间       | X=250–400                       | X=250–320                       |
| 孤立大分配       | X≈430 (~7500 KB)                | X≈400 (~16000 KB)               |
| 总体趋势         | 前期分散，中期集中，后期稀疏    | 前期波动，中期爆发，末期极值    |

---

## 观察结论

1. **“Signing-In” 与 “Open an Account”** 均表现为连续、高频、高幅值的内存分配，表明这些操作涉及大量资源预加载或状态初始化。
2. **“Account Page” 与 “Check&Saving”** 均为单次显著分配，但后者规模更大，暗示其背后数据结构更复杂或需预留更多缓冲空间。
3. 两图中均在 X<100 区间存在若干小型分配，可能是应用启动或基础框架加载所致。
4. 图(b)整体内存使用峰值更高，反映“开户+查存”组合操作比“登录+查看账户”更具资源消耗性。

target.markdown: ## 4.2 攻击 II：用户活动追踪与键盘按键监控

source.markdown: We follow up on the website fingerprinting attack with a user activity tracking and keystroke monitoring attack. The first component of the attack uses a side channel to track the user activity on the web. We define user activity as the navigation to sub-level webpages after a user accesses the main page of a website. For example, a user may sign in or sign up from the main page, or a user may browse through the savings or checking account after logging into the banking webpage. Figure 5 shows two examples of user activity signatures.

target.markdown: 我们在网站指纹识别攻击的基础上，进一步开展了用户活动追踪与键盘按键监控攻击。该攻击的第一个组成部分利用侧信道来追踪用户在网页上的活动。我们将用户活动定义为主页加载之后，用户对子级网页的导航行为。例如，用户可在主页上进行登录或注册，也可在登录网银页面后浏览储蓄账户或支票账户。图 5 展示了两个用户活动签名的示例。

source.markdown: We test this attack on two websites: facebook.com and bankofamerica.com. In the facebook website, our goal is to detect whether the user is signing in or signing up (creating account). In the bankofamerica website, besides detecting signing in/opening an account, we track several user activities to detect which type of account the user intends to open, and other interactions with the website.

target.markdown: 页面访问信息之后，我们可以进一步提取关于用户活动的更细粒度信息。通过反复探测 GPU 内存分配，我们能够检测出用户的输入模式（通常会引起文本框或类似字符动画结构的重新渲染）。更具体地说，从同一信号中，我们可以获得：(1) 受害者所分配的内存大小（粒度为 128KB），借此可判断其是否为用户名/密码输入框（例如，与较大的搜索框相区分）；(2) 按键之间的间隔时间，由此可提取出输入字符的数量，甚至通过时序分析进一步推断出所输入的具体字符。

source.markdown: As an example, we describe the process to infer whether a user is logging in by typing on the password textbox on facebook, as well as to extract the inter-keystroke time of the password input. Since the GPU is not used to render text in the current default options, each time the user types a character, the character itself is rendered by the CPU but the whole password textbox is uploaded to GPU as a texture to be rasterized and composited. In this case, the monitored available memory will decrease with a step of 1024KB (the amount of GPU memory needed to render the password textbox on facebook), leaking the fact that a user is attempting to sign in instead of signing up (where the sign-up textboxes are bigger and require more GPU memory to render). Next, by monitoring the exact time of available memory changes, we infer inter-keystroke time. ### 振荡阶段（事件 9–18）

| 事件编号 | 时间间隔 (ms) | 备注             |
|----------|---------------|------------------|

| 10       | ~220          | 第一个深谷       |

### 最终稳定阶段（事件 19–23）
- 事件 19–23：恢复并稳定在约 600 ms（与初始平台期一致）

- 整体模式：**初始稳定 → 突发下降 → 高频振荡 → 最终回归稳定**
- 最显著特征：在事件 12 处出现极端低延迟（≈100 ms），可能对应某种优化或缓存命中。
- 振荡区间（事件 9–18）显示系统存在周期性资源竞争或垃圾回收行为。
- 起始和结束阶段均维持在 ≈600 ms，表明系统在非扰动状态下具有稳定的响应延迟。

这张图片展示了一个直方图与一条拟合曲线的叠加图，用于可视化“归一化误差”（Normalized error）的概率密度分布。以下是详细的内容提取和分析：

---

## 📊 图表类型
- **组合图**：柱状图（直方图） + 曲线图（概率密度函数拟合）

---

## 📈 坐标轴信息

### X 轴（横轴）
- **标签**：`Normalized error`
- **范围**：从 `-0.1` 到 `0.1`
- **刻度标记**：
  - `-0.1`, `-0.05`, `0`, `0.05`, `0.1`

### Y 轴（纵轴）
- **标签**：`Probability density`
- **范围**：从 `0` 到 `0.32`
- **刻度标记**：
  - `0`, `0.04`, `0.08`, `0.12`, `0.16`, `0.2`, `0.24`, `0.28`, `0.32`

---

## 🟦 直方图（蓝色柱子）

- **颜色**：深蓝色（或海军蓝）
- **用途**：表示归一化误差的样本频率分布（经归一化为概率密度）
- **特征**：
  - 中心集中在 `0` 附近，呈近似对称分布
  - 最高柱位于 `x ≈ 0` 处，高度约 `0.30`
  - 两侧柱子逐渐降低，尾部延伸至约 `±0.07`
  - 在 `x > 0.05` 和 `x < -0.05` 区域仍有少量非零值

---

##  拟合曲线（红色实线）

- **颜色**：红色
- **形状**：钟形曲线，类似正态分布（高斯分布）
- **峰值位置**：略偏右于 `x = 0`，大约在 `x ≈ 0.005~0.01`
- **峰值高度**：约 `0.19`
- **作用**：对直方图数据进行平滑拟合，可能代表理论或经验概率密度函数（如核密度估计或参数化高斯拟合）

> ⚠️ 注意：虽然曲线看起来像高斯分布，但其峰值低于直方图最高柱（0.30 vs 0.19），说明它不是直接匹配直方图最大值，而是整体趋势拟合 —— 可能是经过带宽调整的核密度估计（KDE）。

---

##  数据解读要点

1. **集中性**：
   - 大部分误差集中在 `[-0.05, 0.05]` 区间内
   - 中位数/均值接近 0，表明系统无显著系统性偏差

2. **离散程度**：
   - 标准差可通过曲线宽度估算：半高全宽（FWHM）约为 `0.06~0.08` → σ ≈ FWHM / 2.355 ≈ `0.025~0.034`

3. **尾部行为**：
   - 存在轻微长尾（尤其在右侧 `x > 0.05`），暗示可能存在少数较大正向误差

4. **拟合质量**：
   - 红色曲线未能完全捕捉直方图的尖峰（peakiness），说明实际分布比高斯更陡峭（leptokurtic）
   - 或者拟合时使用了较宽的带宽以平滑噪声

---

## 📌 可能的应用场景

该图常用于以下领域：

- **机器学习模型评估**：预测值与真实值之间的归一化残差分布
- **传感器校准**：测量误差的统计特性分析
- **金融建模**：收益率或预测误差的风险分布
- **工程仿真**：数值模拟结果的误差收敛性检验

---

## ✅ 总结

| 项目             | 描述                                                                 |
|------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 图形内容         | 归一化误差的概率密度直方图 + 红色拟合曲线                            |
| 主要分布特征     | 近似对称、单峰、中心在 0 附近                                        |
| 峰值             | 直方图最高 ~0.30；曲线最高 ~0.19                                     |
| 支持区间         | 主要分布在 [-0.05, 0.05]，极端值可达 ±0.07                           |
| 拟合方法推测     | 核密度估计（KDE）或带偏移的高斯拟合                                  |
| 应用建议         | 可用于误差诊断、置信区间构建、异常检测等                             |

---

## 💡 建议后续操作（若需进一步分析）

1. 计算样本均值、标准差、偏度、峰度
2. 进行 Shapiro-Wilk 或 Kolmogorov-Smirnov 检验判断是否服从正态分布
3. 尝试不同带宽的 KDE 或混合高斯模型（GMM）改进拟合效果
4. 标注关键百分位数（如 95% 置信区间对应的 x 值）

---

source.markdown: To construct the side channel between two computing applications, multiprogramming (the ability to run multiple programs at the same time) on the GPUs needs to be supported. Modern GPUs support multiprogramming through multiple hardware streams with multi-kernel execution either within the same process, or using a multi-process service (MPS) [9], which allows execution of concurrent kernels from different processes on the GPU. MPS is already supported on GPUs with hardware queues such as the Hyper-Q support available on Kepler and newer microarchitecture generations from Nvidia. Multi-process execution eliminates the overhead of GPU context switching and improves the performance, especially when the GPU is underutilized by a single process. The trends in newer generations of GPUs is to expand support for multi-programming; for example, the newest Volta architecture provides hardware support for 32-concurrent address spaces/page tables on the GPU [32]. In fact, all three GPUs we tested for the paper support MPS.

source.markdown: In this attack, our goal is to demonstrate side channels that can be exploited between different computational applications. In this attack scenario, a spy application, perhaps on a cloud, seeks to co-locate on the same GPU as another application to infer its behavior. For the victim, we choose a CUDA-implemented back-propagation algorithm from the Rodinia application benchmark [28]; in such an application, the internal structure of the neural network can be a critical trade secret and the target of model extraction attacks [67].

target.markdown: 在本攻击中，我们的目标是展示可在不同计算应用程序之间被利用的侧信道。在此攻击场景中，一个间谍应用程序（例如位于云端）试图与另一个应用程序共存于同一 GPU 上，以推断其行为。对于受害者，我们从 Rodinia 应用基准 [28] 中选取了一个基于 CUDA 实现的反向传播算法；在这样的应用中，神经网络的内部结构可能构成关键的商业机密，并成为模型提取攻击的目标 [67]。

source.markdown: We use prior results of reverse engineering the hardware schedulers on GPUs [55] to enable a CUDA spy to co-locate with a CUDA victim on each SM. We launch several hundred consecutive kernels in spy to make sure we cover one whole victim kernel execution. These numbers can be scaled up with the length of the victim. To create contention in features tracked by hardware performance counters, the spy accesses different sets of the cache and performs different types of operations on functional units. When a victim is running concurrently on the GPU and utilizing the shared resources, depending on number of input layer size, the intensity and pattern of contention on the cache, memory and functional units is different over time, creating measurable leakage in the spy performance counter measurements. Thus, the spy runs and collects hardware performance counter values over time. We collect one vector of performance counter values from each spy kernel.

source.markdown: We conduct a number of experiments to reverse engineer the GPU schedulers when there are both graphics and computing applications. In the first experiment, we launch a CUDA process and an OpenGL process concurrently on the GPU. On the CUDA side, we write an application to launch a very long CUDA kernel doing some texture memory load operations in a loop and size the application such that there is at least one thread block executing on each SM. We measure the start time and stop time of the CUDA kernel, the start and stop time of each iteration of operations for each thread, and report the SM-ID on which the thread is executing.

In the first experiment, we launch a CUDA process and an OpenGL process concurrently on the GPU. On the CUDA side, we write an application to launch a very long CUDA kernel doing some texture memory load operations in a loop and size the application such that there is at least one thread block executing on each SM. We measure the start time and stop time of the CUDA kernel, the start and stop time of each iteration of operations for each thread, and report the SM-ID on which the thread is executing.

target.markdown: 我们进行了若干实验，以反向推断在同时运行图形应用与计算应用时的 GPU 调度行为。在第一个实验中，我们在 GPU 上同时启动一个 CUDA 进程与一个 OpenGL 进程。在 CUDA 端，我们编写一个应用程序，用于启动一个执行时间很长的 CUDA 内核，该内核在循环中执行一些纹理内存加载操作，并将该应用程序的规模设置为每个 SM 上至少有一个线程块在执行。我们测量 CUDA 内核的启动时间与停止时间、每个线程每轮操作的启动与停止时间，并报告该线程所执行的 SM-ID。

source.markdown: On the OpenGL side, we launch a very long application and probe the execution time and the SM-ID at each pixel (thread) as described in Section 4. From the experiment above, we observed that when the CUDA kernel starts execution, the graphics rendering application is frozen until the CUDA kernel is terminated. So there is no true concurrency between CUDA and OpenGL applications on the GPU SMs. This behavior is different than multiple CUDA applications (or multiple OpenGL applications) which we found to concurrently share the GPU when the resources are sufficient.

source.markdown: Although the same Graphics-Graphics attacks through the memory API can also be implemented through a CUDA spy, we demonstrate a different attack that uses the performance counters. Our attack strategy is that we launch a CUDA spy application including many consecutive short CUDA kernels, in which the threads access the texture memory addresses that are mapped to different sets of texture caches (e.g. each SM on GTX 745 has a 12KB L1 texture cache with 4 sets and 24 ways). To make our attack fast and to optimize the length of each CUDA kernel, we leverage the inherent GPU parallelism to have each thread (or warp) access a unique cache set, so all cache sets are accessed in parallel. Note that number of launched CUDA kernels is selected such that the spy execution time equals to the average rendering time of different websites. The spy kernels collect GPU performance counter values. Although the spy can only see its own performance counter events, the victim execution affects these values due to contention; for example, texture cache hits/misses and global memory events are affected by contention.

target.markdown: 虽然同样基于内存 API 的图形-图形攻击也可以通过 CUDA 间谍程序实施，但我们在此展示一种不同的攻击方法，即使用性能计数器。我们的攻击策略是：启动一个 CUDA 间谍应用程序，其中包含大量连续执行的短 CUDA 内核，这些内核中的线程访问被映射到不同纹理缓存集的纹理内存地址（例如，GTX 745 上每个 SM 拥有一个 12KB 的 L1 纹理缓存，包含 4 个缓存集和 24 路相联）。为了使攻击更加快速并优化每个 CUDA 内核的长度，我们利用 GPU 固有的并行性，使每个线程（或 warp）访问唯一的缓存集，从而所有缓存集能够被并行访问。需要注意的是，所启动的 CUDA 内核数量经过精心选择，使得间谍程序的执行时间等于不同网站的平均渲染时间。间谍内核负责采集 GPU 性能计数器的数值。尽管间谍程序只能观测到自身的性能计数器事件，但由于资源争用，受害者程序的执行会影响这些数值；例如，纹理缓存的命中/未命中以及全局内存事件都会受到争用的影响。

source.markdown: On a CUDA spy application, we launch a large number of consecutive CUDA kernels, each of which accesses different sets of the texture cache using different warps simultaneously at each SM. The intuition is to create contention for these cache sets which are also used by the graphics rendering process. We run our spy and collect performance counter values with each kernel using the Nvidia profiling tools (which are user accessible) while the victim is browsing webpages. Again, we use machine learning to identify the fingerprint of each website using the different signatures observed in the performance counters. We evaluate this attack on 200 top websites on Alexa, and collect 10 samples for each website.

source.markdown: The attack may be mitigated completely by removing the shared resource APIs such as the memory API and the performance counters. However, legitimate applications require the use of these interfaces for uses such as tuning their performance. Thus, our goal is to weaken the signal that the attacker gets, making it harder to infer sensitive information.

target.markdown: 该攻击可以通过移除共享资源 API（如内存 API 和性能计数器）来完全缓解。然而，合法的应用程序需要使用这些接口来进行性能调优等用途。因此，我们的目标是削弱攻击者所获得的信号，使其更难推断出敏感信息。

target.markdown: 我们通过以下方式来评估泄漏的减少：

source.markdown: • Rate limiting: limit the rate an application can call the memory API. In the memory based attack, we can query the API every 60 us (about 16000 times per second), leading to precise identification of memory events corresponding to every object uploaded to the GPU. As we reduce the allowable rate, individual allocation and deallocation events start to be missed, reducing the information in the signal.

blocks.text: • Rate limiting: limit the rate an application can call the memory API. In the memory based attack, we can query the API every 60 us (about 16000 times per second), leading to precise identification of memory events corresponding to every object uploaded to the GPU. As we reduce the allowable rate, individual allocation and deallocation events start to be missed, reducing the information in the signal.

target.markdown: • **速率限制**：限制应用程序调用内存 API 的速率。在基于内存的攻击中，我们可以每隔 60 微秒（约每秒 16000 次）查询一次 API，从而精确识别出与每个上传到 GPU 的对象相对应的内存事件。随着我们将允许的查询速率降低，单次分配与释放事件开始出现遗漏，从而减少了信号中的信息量。

source.markdown: • Precision limiting: limit the granularity of the measurement. For example, for the memory API, we set a granularity (e.g., 4Mbytes) and report the memory allocation rounded up to this granularity. Small size allocations can be missed, and the precise size of allocations becomes unknown, weakening the signal.

target.markdown: • **精度限制**：限制测量的粒度。例如，对于内存 API，我们设定一个粒度（例如 4 Mbytes），并将内存分配量向上取整到该粒度后进行报告。较小尺寸的分配可能会被遗漏，且分配的精确大小将变得未知，从而削弱信号。

source.markdown: defense as shown in Figure 9a, but its success is limited (as 40% precision can still be achieved under aggressive rate limit). We repeat the experiments approach as we reduce the precision of the reported available memory. In our experiments, for full screen window size, the smallest and most memory allocations on GPU for different websites are 128 KB. If we decrease the granularity and bin all memory allocations to 512KB, 1024KB, 2048KB and 4096KB, the precision of retrained model will be decreased as shown in Figure 9b. By decreasing the granularity to 8192KB, the accuracy will be significantly decreased to about 7%. By combining the two mentioned approaches, using 4096KB granularity and limiting the query rate we can further decrease the precision to almost 4%, as demonstrated in Figure 9c. While reducing precision, we believe these mitigations retain some information for legitimate applications to measure their performance, while preventing side channel leakage across applications.

target.markdown: 如图 9a 所示，速率限制可以降低分类精确度，但其效果有限（即便在较为激进的速率限制下，精确度仍能达到 40%）。我们在降低所报告可用内存精度的过程中重复了上述实验。在我们的实验中，对于全屏窗口大小，不同网站在 GPU 上的最小和最常见的内存分配为 128 KB。如果我们将粒度降低，并将所有内存分配按 512KB、1024KB、2048KB 和 4096KB 进行分箱，重新训练模型的精确度将如图 9b 所示下降。当粒度降低至 8192KB 时，准确率将显著下降至约 7%。通过将两种方法相结合——使用 4096KB 的粒度并限制查询速率——我们可以将精确度进一步降低至接近 4%，如图 9c 所示。尽管这降低了精确度，但我们认为这些缓解措施仍能为合法应用程序保留一部分用于测量自身性能的信息，同时防止跨应用的侧信道泄漏。

source.markdown: To further evaluate the rate limiting mitigation, we abuse the memory API to implement a covert channel and investigate performance of covert channel with and without the mitigation. To construct the covert channel, a spy application queries the memory API repeatedly to probe the available memory on GPU and detect new memory allocations. On the other side, a trojan application allocates a constant amount of memory on GPU to send "1" and does nothing to send "0". Without any mitigation in place, the achievable covert channel bandwidth is as high as 4Kbps, while rate limiting mitigation decreases the bandwidth to about 910bps, 98bps and 2bps for 1000/s, 100/s and 2/s cases respectively.

source.markdown: Different attack vectors have been proposed for website fingerprinting. Panchenko et al. [60] and Hayes et al. [38] capture traffic generated via loading monitored web pages and feed the traces to machine learning based classification. Felten and Schneider [35] utilize browser caching and construct a timing channel to infer the victim visited websites. Jana and Shmatikov [39] use the *procfs* filesystem in Linux to measure the memory footprints of the browser. Then they detect the visited website by comparing the memory footprints with the recorded ones. Weinberg et al. [70] presented a user interaction attack (victim's action on website leaks its browsing history) and a timing side channel attack for browser history sniffing.

target.markdown: 针对网站指纹攻击，研究者提出了多种不同的攻击向量。Panchenko 等人 [60] 与 Hayes 等人 [38] 通过采集受监控网页加载过程中产生的网络流量，并将其输入基于机器学习的分类器进行识别。Felten 和 Schneider [35] 利用浏览器缓存机制构建了一条时间信道，从而推断受害者访问过的网站。Jana 和 Shmatikov [39] 则使用 Linux 中的 *procfs* 文件系统来测量浏览器的内存占用情况，随后将所测得的内存占用与预先记录的轮廓进行比对，从而检测受害者访问过的网站。Weinberg 等人 [70] 提出了一种用户交互攻击（受害者对网站的操作会泄漏其浏览历史）以及一种用于嗅探浏览器历史的时间侧信道攻击。

source.markdown: Some of the principles used in our attack have also been leveraged by other researchers. Gothem et al. [68] and Bortz et al. [26] propose cross-site timing attacks on web browsers to estimate the size of cross-origin resources or provide user information leakage from other site. [66] and [45] propose timing channels by measuring the time elapsed between frames using a JavaScript API. Kotcher et al. [45] found that after applying CSS filter to framed document, its rendering time becomes related to its content. Similarly, Stone et al. [66] either detect the redraw events or measure the time of applying the SVG filter to perform history sniffing. These attacks are difficult currently since most browsers have reduced the timer resolution eliminating the timing signal used by the attacks. Oren et al. [59] implement a last level cache prime+probe side channel in JavaScript. More recently, Vila and Kopf [69] present a side channel attack on shared event loop in which the attacker enqueues several short tasks, and records the time these tasks are scheduled. The time difference between two consecutive tasks reveals the existence of the victim and duration of its task. Gulmezoglu et al. [37] proposed a side channel on per-core/per-process CPU hardware performance counters (which are limited in number). Zhang et al. [72] identify several iOS APIs as attack vectors to implement cross-app information leakage to extract private user information, detecting installed apps, etc. All of these attack models are proposed at browser/OS level or CPU hardware level, providing different attack vector than our attacks which target the GPU hardware to extract sensitive information through side channels.

target.markdown: 我们攻击中所采用的某些原理也已被其他研究者所利用。Gothem 等人 [68] 与 Bortz 等人 [26] 针对 Web 浏览器提出了跨站点时间攻击，用以推断跨源资源的大小或泄漏其他站点的用户信息。[66] 和 [45] 则利用 JavaScript API 通过测量帧之间所经过的时间来构建时间信道。Kotcher 等人 [45] 发现，对框架文档施加 CSS 滤镜后，其渲染时间会与内容相关联。类似地，Stone 等人 [66] 通过检测重绘事件或测量施加 SVG 滤镜所耗费的时间来执行历史记录嗅探。这些攻击目前已难以实施，因为大多数浏览器都已降低了定时器精度，从而消除了攻击所依赖的时间信号。Oren 等人 [59] 在 JavaScript 中实现了一种末级缓存 prime+probe 侧信道攻击。近年来，Vila 和 Kopf [69] 提出了一种针对共享事件循环的侧信道攻击，攻击者通过入队若干短任务，并记录这些任务被调度执行的时间。相邻两个任务之间的时间差能够揭示受害者的存在及其任务的持续时间。Gulmezoglu 等人 [37] 针对每核/每进程 CPU 硬件性能计数器（其数量有限）提出了一种侧信道攻击。Zhang 等人 [72] 识别出多种 iOS API 可作为攻击向量，用以实现跨应用信息泄漏，从而提取用户的隐私信息、检测已安装的应用等。所有这些攻击模型均是在浏览器/操作系统层面或 CPU 硬件层面提出的，所提供的攻击向量与我们以 GPU 硬件为目标、通过侧信道提取敏感信息的攻击有所不同。

source.markdown: Leakage through the keystroke timing pattern is also a known effect which has been exploited as a user authentication mechanism  $ [30, 53, 61] $ . Keystroke timing has also been used to compromise/weaken passwords  $ [65] $  or compromise user privacy  $ [27] $ . Lipp et al.  $ [47] $  propose a keystroke interrupt-timing attack implemented in JavaScript using a counter as a high resolution timer. Our attack provides an accurate new leakage of keystroke timing to unauthorized users enabling them to implement such attacks. We demonstrated that GPU side channels threaten not only graphics applications, but also computational workloads running on GPU.

source.text: 8.2 Side Channel Attacks on GPUs

blocks.text: 8.2 Side Channel Attacks on GPUs

target.markdown: # 8.2 针对 GPU 的侧信道攻击

source.markdown: Jiang et al. [40] conduct a timing attack on a CUDA AES implementation. The attack exploits the difference in timing between addresses generated by different threads as they access memory: if the addresses are coalesced such that they refer to the same memory block, they are much faster than uncoalesced accesses which require several expensive memory operations. Thus, in a GPU implemented cryptographic application, the key affects the address pattern accessed by the threads, and therefore the observed run time of the encryption algorithm, opening the door for a timing attack where the encryption time is used to infer the likely key. The same group [41] presented another timing attack on table-based AES encryption. They found correlation between execution time of one table lookup of a warp and a number of bank conflicts generated by threads within the warp. The attacks require the spy to be able to trigger the launch of the victim kernel. The self-contention exploited in the first attack [40] cannot be used for a side-channel between two concurrent applications. Moreover, these attacks are only used to exploit a CUDA victim. Luo et al. study a power side channel attack on AES encryption executing on a GPU [49]. This attack requires physical access to the GPU to measure the power.

target.markdown: Jiang 等人 [40] 对一种 CUDA AES 实现进行了时间攻击。该攻击利用不同线程访问内存时所生成地址之间的时间差异：若地址经过合并而指向同一内存块，则访问速度远快于需要多次昂贵内存操作的未合并访问。因此，在 GPU 上实现的密码学应用中，密钥会影响线程所访问的地址模式，进而影响加密算法的实际运行时间，这为通过加密时间推断可能密钥的时间攻击打开了大门。同一研究团队 [41] 还针对基于查表的 AES 加密提出了另一种时间攻击。他们发现 warp 中单次查表的执行时间与该 warp 内线程所引发的存储体冲突数量之间存在相关性。这些攻击均要求攻击者能够触发受害者内核的启动。[40] 中所利用的自我争用无法用于两个并发应用之间的侧信道。此外，这些攻击仅可用于利用 CUDA 受害者。Luo 等人 [49] 研究了针对 GPU 上 AES 加密的功耗侧信道攻击。该攻击需要物理接触 GPU 以测量其功耗。

source.markdown: Naghibijouybari et al. [55] construct three types of covert channels between two colluding CUDA applications. We use their results for reverse engineering the co-location of CUDA workloads in our third attack on the neural network application. The fine-grained timing information that they use in a covert channel by enforcing regular contention patterns is too noisy to exploit for side-channel attacks due to the large number of active threads.

source.markdown: This work is the first that explores side channels due to contention between two GPU applications. It is also the only GPU attack to compromise graphics applications; prior works consider CUDA applications only. Many side channel attacks have been proposed on CPUs; our memory API attack bears similarity to side channel attacks through proofs [29, 39]. Our defense mechanism is in the spirit of other side channel defenses that limit the leakage by interfering with the measurement APIs [50, 72].

source.markdown: # 9 CONCLUDING REMARKS
source.text: 9 CONCLUDING REMARKS

blocks.text: 9 CONCLUDING REMARKS

target.markdown: # 9 结论

source.markdown: In this paper, we explore side channel attacks among applications concurrently using the Graphical Processing Unit (GPU). We reverse engineer how applications share of the GPU for different threat scenarios and also identify different ways to measure leakage. We demonstrate a series of end-to-end GPU side channel attacks covering the different threat scenarios on both graphics and computational stacks, as well as across them. The first attack implements website fingerprinting through GPU memory utilization API or GPU performance counters. We extend this attack to track user activities as they interact with a website or type characters on a keyboard. We can accurately track re-rendering events on GPU and measure the timing of keystrokes as they type characters in a textbox (e.g., a password box), making it possible to carry out keystroke timing analysis to infer the characters being typed by the user.

target.markdown: 在本文中，我们探索了并发使用图形处理器（GPU）的应用程序之间的侧信道攻击。我们逆向分析了应用程序在不同的威胁场景下共享 GPU 的方式，并识别出了多种测量泄漏的途径。我们展示了一系列端到端的 GPU 侧信道攻击，涵盖了图形栈与计算栈之上、之间以及跨栈的多种威胁场景。第一种攻击通过 GPU 内存使用率 API 或 GPU 性能计数器实现网站指纹识别。我们将该攻击进一步扩展，用以追踪用户在浏览网站或在键盘上输入字符时的活动。我们能够精确地追踪 GPU 上的重绘事件，并测量用户在文本框（例如密码框）中输入字符时的按键时间间隔，从而使得实施按键时序分析以推断用户所输入字符成为可能。

source.markdown: A second attack uses a CUDA spy to infer the internal structure of a neural network application from the Rodinia benchmark, demonstrating that these attacks are also dangerous on the cloud. We believe that this class of attacks represents a substantial new threat targeting sensitive GPU-accelerated computational (e.g. deep neural networks) and graphics (e.g. web browsers) workloads.

source.markdown: The paper also considered possible defenses. We proposed a mitigation based on limiting the rate of access to the APIs that leak the side channel information. Alternatively (or in combination), we can reduce the precision of this information. We showed that such defenses substantially reduce the effectiveness of the attack, to the point where the attacks are no longer effective. Finding the right balance between utility and side channel leakage for general applications is an interesting tradeoff to study for this class of mitigations.
